Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

1	// Package authz is the permission service: the durable, per-document and
2	// per-device authorization ledger together with the system's single revoke
3	// verdict.
4	//
5	// Every (document, device) pair starts authorized; a grant or revoke is
6	// recorded per pair. The lookup and the write run in one serialized
7	// transaction on the shared connection and commit to disk, so concurrent
8	// grant/revoke calls each land as a complete state and survive a restart.
9	//
10	// The other services do not read the permission table. They take their
11	// registration-and-authorization verdict through AuthorizedTx, evaluated
12	// inside their own write transaction, so a rejected request is judged before
13	// any document content is observed and the gate and the gated work commit as
14	// one judgment. Revoking never deletes changes, snapshots, sessions or CRDT
15	// state; it only produces the denial and, after the revoke commits, notifies
16	// the registered revoke sinks (the live subscription registries) so they can
17	// end the affected connections with the one-time, sticky 4403 close.
18	package authz
19	
20	import (
21		"database/sql"
22		"errors"
23		"sync"
24	
25		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
26	)
27	
28	// schema is created when the service is constructed; its shape is unchanged
29	// from the pre-refactor layout, so authorization rows already on disk stay
30	// readable.
31	const schema = `
32	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS document_permissions (
33		document_id TEXT NOT NULL,
34		device_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
35		authorized  INTEGER NOT NULL,
36		PRIMARY KEY (document_id, device_id)
37	);
38	`
39	
40	// RevokeSink observes a committed revoke. The change event service and the
41	// CRDT service register themselves to end the affected live subscriptions; a
42	// sink must not block and must be safe to call after the revoke transaction
43	// has committed. The permission service depends on this interface alone, so
44	// the dependency points from the observers toward the verdict and never back.
45	type RevokeSink interface {
46		PermissionRevoked(documentID, deviceID string)
47	}
48	
49	// Service is the permission service.
50	type Service struct {
51		db *sql.DB
52	
53		mu    sync.Mutex
54		sinks []RevokeSink
55	}
56	
57	// New constructs the permission service over the shared kernel handle and
58	// creates its table.
59	func New(kernel *store.Store) (*Service, error) {
60		db := kernel.DB()
61		if _, err := db.Exec(schema); err != nil {
62			return nil, err
63		}
64		return &Service{db: db}, nil
65	}
66	
67	// AddRevokeSink registers an observer notified after every committed revoke.
68	// It is called by the composition root while wiring the services, before the
69	// surface serves requests.
70	func (s *Service) AddRevokeSink(sink RevokeSink) {
71		s.mu.Lock()
72		s.sinks = append(s.sinks, sink)
73		s.mu.Unlock()
74	}
75	
76	// AuthorizedTx is the shared gate: it returns nil when deviceID is registered
77	// and currently authorized for documentID, store.ErrDeviceNotFound when the
78	// device is not registered and store.ErrPermissionDenied when its access has
79	// been revoked. It runs inside the caller's transaction q, so the verdict is
80	// taken on the same serialized connection as the work it guards, before any
81	// document content is read.
82	func (s *Service) AuthorizedTx(q store.DBTX, documentID, deviceID string) error {
83		exists, err := store.DeviceExistsTx(q, deviceID)
84		if err != nil {
85			return err
86		}
87		if !exists {
88			return store.ErrDeviceNotFound
89		}
90		var stored int
91		err = q.QueryRow(
92			`SELECT authorized FROM document_permissions WHERE document_id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
93			documentID, deviceID,
94		).Scan(&stored)
95		switch {
96		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
97			// No deviation row: devices start authorized.
98			return nil
99		case err != nil:
100			return err
101		default:
102			if stored == 0 {
103				return store.ErrPermissionDenied
104			}
105			return nil
106		}
107	}
108	
109	// DeviceAuthorizedTx adapts the shared gate to the change event and CRDT
110	// services' Gate interface (which names *sql.Tx). The verdict is identical.
111	func (s *Service) DeviceAuthorizedTx(tx *sql.Tx, documentID, deviceID string) error {
112		return s.AuthorizedTx(tx, documentID, deviceID)
113	}
114	
115	// SetDocumentPermission grants or revokes deviceID's access to documentID and
116	// reports whether the stored permission actually changed.
117	//
118	// Every device starts authorized for every document, so the first revoke is
119	// the first write for the pair (changed=true); repeating a state that already
120	// holds writes nothing and reports changed=false. An unregistered device
121	// yields store.ErrDeviceNotFound and nothing is written. The lookup and the
122	// write run in one serialized transaction, so concurrent grant/revoke calls
123	// each commit completely and the final state matches the last committed
124	// action. After a revoke commits, every registered sink is notified; a grant
125	// notifies nothing (a prior revoke already ended the connection stickily).
126	func (s *Service) SetDocumentPermission(documentID, deviceID string, authorized bool) (changed bool, err error) {
127		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
128		if err != nil {
129			return false, err
130		}
131		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
132	
133		exists, err := store.DeviceExistsTx(tx, deviceID)
134		if err != nil {
135			return false, err
136		}
137		if !exists {
138			return false, store.ErrDeviceNotFound
139		}
140	
141		current := true // devices start authorized; a row only records a deviation
142		var stored int
143		err = tx.QueryRow(
144			`SELECT authorized FROM document_permissions WHERE document_id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
145			documentID, deviceID,
146		).Scan(&stored)
147		switch {
148		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
149			// No row: the default (authorized) holds.
150		case err != nil:
151			return false, err
152		default:
153			current = stored != 0
154		}
155		if current == authorized {
156			return false, tx.Commit()
157		}
158	
159		v := 0
160		if authorized {
161			v = 1
162		}
163		if _, err := tx.Exec(
164			`INSERT INTO document_permissions (document_id, device_id, authorized) VALUES (?, ?, ?)
165			 ON CONFLICT (document_id, device_id) DO UPDATE SET authorized = excluded.authorized`,
166			documentID, deviceID, v,
167		); err != nil {
168			return false, err
169		}
170		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
171			return false, err
172		}
173	
174		// A grant cannot unblock a subscription (the first revoke already ended
175		// it, stickily); only a revoke needs to end live subscriptions.
176		if !authorized {
177			s.mu.Lock()
178			sinks := append([]RevokeSink(nil), s.sinks...)
179			s.mu.Unlock()
180			for _, sink := range sinks {
181				sink.PermissionRevoked(documentID, deviceID)
182			}
183		}
184		return true, nil
185	}
186	
187	// DeleteDevicePermissionsTx removes every document-permission ledger row that
188	// names deviceID, inside the caller's transaction: grants and revokes the
189	// deregistered device held on documents vanish together with the device. It is
190	// the permission service's share of device deregistration, run in the same
191	// serialized transaction as the registration layer's cascade, so the row
192	// removals and the device deletion commit as one judgment. After the device
193	// row is gone the default verdict would be "unregistered" anyway; clearing the
194	// rows guarantees a device that later re-registers the same id starts with no
195	// inherited authorization state.
196	func (s *Service) DeleteDevicePermissionsTx(q store.DBTX, deviceID string) error {
197		_, err := q.Exec(
198			`DELETE FROM document_permissions WHERE device_id = ?`, deviceID,
199		)
200		return err
201	}
202	
203	// DocumentAuthorized reports whether deviceID currently holds permission for
204	// documentID. Devices start authorized, so an absent row means authorized.
205	func (s *Service) DocumentAuthorized(documentID, deviceID string) (bool, error) {
206		var stored int
207		err := s.db.QueryRow(
208			`SELECT authorized FROM document_permissions WHERE document_id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
209			documentID, deviceID,
210		).Scan(&stored)
211		switch {
212		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
213			return true, nil
214		case err != nil:
215			return false, err
216		default:
217			return stored != 0, nil
218		}
219	}

82	// NewHandlerWithReadiness builds the same public HTTP surface as NewHandler but
83	// answers every request — including GET /healthz — with a 503 JSON error until
84	// ready reports that the database is open and the listener is accepting
85	// connections. Once ready, responses are byte-for-byte what NewHandler emits;
86	// readiness is one-way, so a later flip back is not part of the contract.
87	func NewHandlerWithReadiness(s *app.App, ready func() bool) http.Handler {
88		h := NewHandler(s)
89		if ready == nil {
90			return h
91		}
92		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
93			if !ready() {
94				writeError(w, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "service is not ready")
95				return
96			}
97			h.ServeHTTP(w, r)
98		})
99	}

101	// NewHandler builds the public HTTP surface backed by s.
102	func NewHandler(s *app.App) http.Handler {
103		mux := http.NewServeMux()
104	
105		mux.HandleFunc("GET /healthz", func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
106			writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"status": "ok"})
107		})
108	
109		mux.HandleFunc("POST /v1/devices", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
110			handleRegisterDevice(s, w, r)
111		})
112		mux.HandleFunc("DELETE /v1/devices/{deviceId}", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
113			handleDeregisterDevice(s, w, r)
114		})
115		// The device item path accepts only DELETE (deregistration); every other
116		// verb gets a JSON 400 rather than the subtree's unknown-path JSON 404.
117		mux.HandleFunc("/v1/devices/{deviceId}", func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
118			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "method is not allowed on this path")
119		})
120		// A DELETE short of the device id misses the segment that names the
121		// deregistering device; answer a JSON 400 instead of the collection's
122		// unknown-path JSON 404.
123		mux.HandleFunc("DELETE /v1/devices", func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
124			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "device deregistration path is malformed")
125		})
126		// Non-POST verbs on the exact collection path: the method-less pattern is
127		// less specific than POST above, so it only catches the rest and answers a
128		// JSON 404 instead of ServeMux's slash redirect. The explicit DELETE
129		// pattern above wins for a bodyless deregistration missing its id segment.

376	// emptyIDGuard rejects requests carrying an empty path identifier with a 400
377	// JSON error instead of letting ServeMux emit its HTML redirect or a
378	// plain-text 404.
379	//
380	// The document family keeps its original rule (an empty documentID, i.e. the
381	// prefix /v1/documents//); other odd paths there retain their old response so
382	// the pre-existing surface is unchanged. The new device/session families are
383	// stricter: any doubled slash (an empty deviceId, sessionId or documentId
384	// segment) or a trailing slash (an empty final id) is a 400 JSON error.
385	func emptyIDGuard(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
386		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
387			p := r.URL.Path
388	
389			documentSegmentEmpty := strings.HasPrefix(p, "/v1/documents//")
390			newFamilySegmentEmpty := false
391			if strings.HasPrefix(p, "/v1/devices/") || strings.HasPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/") {
392				newFamilySegmentEmpty = strings.Contains(p, "//") || strings.HasSuffix(p, "/")
393			}
394	
395			if documentSegmentEmpty || newFamilySegmentEmpty || malformedNewDocumentPath(p) || malformedSubscribePath(p) || malformedSessionCRDTPath(p) || malformedCRDTPath(p) || malformedSnapshotPath(p) {
396				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "path identifiers must be non-empty strings")
397				return
398			}
399			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
400		})
401	}

403	// malformedNewDocumentPath reports whether p targets one of the new
404	// long-poll/replay/compaction endpoints but is not that endpoint's exact
405	// location: a missing/empty segment, a trailing slash, extra segments, or a
406	// "poll"/"replay"/"compact" segment in a position short of the registered
407	// shape. ServeMux would answer those with a 301 redirect or a plain-text
408	// 404/405; the new endpoints promise a JSON error and never a redirect, so
409	// every such path is a malformed 400.
410	//
411	// Keywords are matched only past the documentID position, so documents that
412	// happen to be named "poll", "replay" or "compact" keep their ordinary
413	// merge/snapshot/changes routes.
414	func malformedNewDocumentPath(p string) bool {
415		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/documents/")
416		if !ok {
417			return false
418		}
419		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
420	
421		// Poll endpoint: "poll" must be exactly the third segment, after a
422		// non-empty documentID and "changes".
423		for i, seg := range segs {
424			if seg == "poll" && i > 0 {
425				return !(len(segs) == 3 && segs[0] != "" && segs[1] == "changes")
426			}
427		}
428		// Replay endpoint: "replay" must be exactly the second segment, after a
429		// non-empty documentID.
430		for i, seg := range segs {
431			if seg == "replay" && i > 0 {
432				return !(len(segs) == 2 && segs[0] != "")
433			}
434		}
435		// Compaction endpoint: "compact" must be exactly the third segment, after
436		// a non-empty documentID and "changes". The CRDT namespace has its own
437		// guard; "compact" there is the CRDT compaction keyword, not the
438		// change-log one.
439		for i, seg := range segs {
440			if seg == "compact" && i > 0 {
441				if len(segs) >= 2 && segs[1] == "crdt" {
442					return false
443				}
444				return !(len(segs) == 3 && segs[0] != "" && segs[1] == "changes")
445			}
446		}
447		return false
448	}

450	// malformedSubscribePath reports whether p targets the WebSocket subscription
451	// endpoint but is not at its exact location
452	// (/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/changes/subscribe): a
453	// missing "documents"/"changes" segment, an extra segment, or a "subscribe"
454	// segment short of the registered shape. ServeMux would answer those with a
455	// plain-text 404/405; every failure of this endpoint must be a JSON 400
456	// instead. Empty segments are already rejected by the guard itself.
457	//
458	// "subscribe" is treated as the endpoint keyword only in the endpoint's
459	// terminal segment position (the fifth segment, index 4); a session or
460	// document identifier literally named "subscribe" occupies an identifier
461	// position (index 0 or 2) and is therefore left to the ordinary
462	// changes/subscribe routes like any other id.
463	func malformedSubscribePath(p string) bool {
464		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/")
465		if !ok {
466			return false
467		}
468		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
469		// The CRDT namespace ("crdt" immediately past the document identifier)
470		// has its own guard; "subscribe" there is not the changes-subscribe
471		// keyword.
472		if len(segs) >= 4 && segs[1] == "documents" && segs[3] == "crdt" {
473			return false
474		}
475		for i, seg := range segs {
476			if seg != "subscribe" {
477				continue
478			}
479			// Identifier positions: sessionId (0) and documentId (2). A value of
480			// "subscribe" there is an ordinary identifier, not the endpoint word.
481			if i == 0 || i == 2 {
482				continue
483			}
484			// Endpoint keyword position: the fifth segment must be exactly
485			// "subscribe" with the documents/changes scaffolding around it, and no
486			// segment may follow. Any other occurrence is a malformed path.
487			if i == 4 && len(segs) == 5 &&
488				segs[0] != "" &&
489				segs[1] == "documents" &&
490				segs[2] != "" &&
491				segs[3] == "changes" {
492				return false
493			}
494			return true
495		}
496		return false
497	}

499	// malformedSessionCRDTPath reports whether p targets the session-scoped CRDT
500	// namespace but is not at one of its two exact locations:
501	//
502	//	GET /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/state
503	//	GET /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/state/subscribe
504	//
505	// a missing "state"/"subscribe" segment, an extra segment, or a "crdt" segment
506	// in the keyword position (immediately past the document identifier) short of
507	// one of the registered shapes. ServeMux would answer those with a
508	// plain-text 404/405; every failure of these endpoints must be a JSON 400
509	// instead. Empty segments are already rejected by the guard itself.
510	//
511	// "crdt" is treated as the endpoint keyword only in the fourth segment (index
512	// 3, right after the document identifier); a session or document identifier
513	// literally named "crdt" occupies an identifier position (index 0 or 2) and
514	// keeps its ordinary routes.
515	func malformedSessionCRDTPath(p string) bool {
516		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/")
517		if !ok {
518			return false
519		}
520		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
521		if len(segs) < 4 || segs[1] != "documents" || segs[3] != "crdt" {
522			return false
523		}
524		// Keyword position reached. The state read is exactly
525		// {sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/state; the subscription adds
526		// one trailing "subscribe" segment.
527		validState := len(segs) == 5 &&
528			segs[0] != "" &&
529			segs[2] != "" &&
530			segs[4] == "state"
531		validSubscribe := len(segs) == 6 &&
532			segs[0] != "" &&
533			segs[2] != "" &&
534			segs[4] == "state" &&
535			segs[5] == "subscribe"
536		return !(validState || validSubscribe)
537	}

549	// decodeJSONBody enforces the strict POST contract shared by every JSON
550	// endpoint: Content-Type must be application/json, the body is capped at
551	// maxBatchBytes, it must contain exactly one JSON value, and no trailing data
552	// may follow it. Any violation writes a 400 JSON error and returns false; the
553	// caller returns immediately, so no handler reaches the store with malformed
554	// input and rejected requests write nothing.
555	func decodeJSONBody(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, dst any) bool {
556		mediaType, _, err := mime.ParseMediaType(r.Header.Get("Content-Type"))
557		if err != nil || mediaType != "application/json" {
558			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "Content-Type must be application/json")
559			return false
560		}
561	
562		r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxBatchBytes)
563		dec := json.NewDecoder(r.Body)
564		if err := dec.Decode(dst); err != nil {
565			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body: "+err.Error())
566			return false
567		}
568		// Reject trailing data after the JSON value.
569		if err := dec.Decode(&struct{}{}); !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
570			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body: unexpected trailing content")
571			return false
572		}
573		return true
574	}

979	// parseCursorPath reports whether raw is a decimal non-negative integer and
980	// returns its value. Signs, fractions and other adornments are rejected.
981	func parseCursorPath(raw string) (int64, bool) {
982		if raw == "" {
983			return 0, false
984		}
985		for _, c := range raw {
986			if c < '0' || c > '9' {
987				return 0, false
988			}
989		}
990		n, err := strconv.ParseInt(raw, 10, 64)
991		if err != nil {
992			return 0, false
993		}
994		return n, true
995	}

997	// parseNonNegativeInt reports whether raw is a JSON integer >= 0. Floats,// strings, booleans, null and negative numbers are rejected.
998	func parseNonNegativeInt(raw json.RawMessage) (int64, bool) {
999		var n int64
1000		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &n); err != nil || n < 0 {
1001			return 0, false
1002		}
1003		// Guard against values like 1.0 that Unmarshal into int64 on some inputs;
1004		// require the literal to contain no fraction or exponent.
1005		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(string(raw))
1006		if trimmed == "" || trimmed[0] == '-' {
1007			return 0, false
1008		}
1009		for _, c := range trimmed {
1010			if c < '0' || c > '9' {
1011				return 0, false
1012			}
1013		}
1014		return n, true
1015	}
1016	
1017	// parsePositiveInt reports whether raw is a JSON integer >= 1. Zero, floats,
1018	// strings, booleans, null and negative numbers are rejected.
1019	func parsePositiveInt(raw json.RawMessage) (int64, bool) {
1020		n, ok := parseNonNegativeInt(raw)
1021		if !ok || n < 1 {
1022			return 0, false
1023		}
1024		return n, true
1025	}
1026	
1027	// isJSONObject reports whether raw decodes to a JSON object (not null, an
1028	// array or a scalar).
1029	func isJSONObject(raw json.RawMessage) bool {
1030		var m map[string]json.RawMessage
1031		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &m); err != nil || m == nil {
1032			return false
1033		}
1034		return true
1035	}

1149	// handlePollChanges is the long-polling entry over the change log.
1150	//
1151	// Query params share the existing change-read constraints: after is a
1152	// non-negative cursor (default 0) and limit is 1..1000 (default 100); waitMs
1153	// is 0..30000 (default 0). Rows already past after return immediately; a known
1154	// document caught up to after parks until the first new commit or the wait
1155	// deadline; an unknown document returns an empty page with cursor 0 at once.
1156	// The response shape is the ordinary page plus a timedOut flag; a deadline
1157	// expiry echoes the caller's cursor and never advances it. A client
1158	// disconnect simply stops the wait and writes nothing.
1159	func handlePollChanges(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
1160		documentID := r.PathValue("documentID") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1161	
1162		after, limit, ok := parseChangesQuery(w, r)
1163		if !ok {
1164			return
1165		}
1166		q := r.URL.Query()
1167		var waitMs int64
1168		if raw := q.Get("waitMs"); raw != "" {
1169			v, err := strconv.ParseInt(raw, 10, 64)
1170			if err != nil || v < 0 || v > maxPollWaitMillis {
1171				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "waitMs must be an integer between 0 and 30000")
1172				return
1173			}
1174			waitMs = v
1175		}
1176	
1177		changes, nextCursor, timedOut, err := s.WaitForChanges(
1178			r.Context(), documentID, after, limit, time.Duration(waitMs)*time.Millisecond,
1179		)
1180		switch {
1181		case errors.Is(err, events.ErrStoreClosing):
1182			writeError(w, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "service is shutting down")
1183			return
1184		case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled), errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded):
1185			// The client went away (or, with waitMs bounded, its deadline lapsed
1186			// at the transport): nothing more to write and nothing was stored.
1187			return
1188		case err != nil:
1189			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to poll changes")
1190			return
1191		}
1192	
1193		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{
1194			"changes":    changes,
1195			"nextCursor": nextCursor,
1196			"timedOut":   timedOut,
1197		})
1198	}
1199	
1200	// handleReplay retries an offline batch against the existing change log. The
1201	// request and per-element semantics mirror POST .../changes — strict
1202	// application/json body, non-empty ids, no in-batch duplicates, idempotent only
1203	// when deviceId and decoded payload match, otherwise 409 reporting the
1204	// conflicting id — with the registration/permission layer enforced first:
1205	// 404 for an unregistered device and 403 for a revoked one, neither exposing
1206	// change content. The whole batch commits in one serialized transaction that
1207	// shares the document's contiguous cursor space with ordinary commits.
1208	func handleReplay(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
1209		documentID := r.PathValue("documentID") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
1210	
1211		var req replayRequest
1212		if !decodeJSONBody(w, r, &req) {
1213			return
1214		}
1215		if req.DeviceID == "" {
1216			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "deviceId must be a non-empty string")
1217			return
1218		}
1219		if req.Operations == nil {
1220			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "operations must be a non-empty array")
1221			return
1222		}
1223		if len(req.Operations) == 0 {
1224			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "operations must be a non-empty array")
1225			return
1226		}
1227	
1228		changes := make([]events.Change, len(req.Operations))
1229		seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(req.Operations))
1230		for i, op := range req.Operations {
1231			if op.ID == "" {
1232				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each operation must have a non-empty string id")
1233				return
1234			}
1235			if len(op.Payload) == 0 {
1236				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "each operation must carry a JSON payload")
1237				return
1238			}
1239			if _, dup := seen[op.ID]; dup {
1240				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "duplicate operation id within batch: "+op.ID)
1241				return
1242			}
1243			seen[op.ID] = struct{}{}
1244			changes[i] = events.Change{ID: op.ID, DeviceID: req.DeviceID, Payload: op.Payload}
1245		}
1246	
1247		results, err := s.ReplayChanges(documentID, changes)
1248		if err != nil {
1249			var conflict *events.ErrConflict
1250			switch {
1251			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDeviceNotFound):
1252				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "device not found")
1253			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrPermissionDenied):
1254				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "device permission for this document has been revoked")
1255			case errors.As(err, &conflict):
1256				writeJSON(w, http.StatusConflict, map[string]string{
1257					"error":      "operation id already exists with different deviceId or payload",
1258					"conflictId": conflict.ID,
1259				})
1260			default:
1261				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to replay operations")
1262			}
1263			return
1264		}
1265	
1266		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"results": results})
1267	}

109	// declared total size and chunk size (positive integers) and the lowercase

116

162	// handlePutChunk stores one binary chunk of an upload. The request must be
163	// application/octet-stream; the index is zero-based and chunks may arrive in
164	// any order. An unknown attachment is a 404 and a non-creator device a 403; a
165	// wrong content type, an out-of-range index, a short non-final chunk or a
166	// final chunk beyond the declared total is a 400 — none of these write
167	// anything. Re-submitting identical bytes is idempotent; different bytes for

169	// finished it is sealed: every further chunk write, even a byte-identical
170	// one, is a 409 and the stored content is unchanged.

172		deviceID := r.PathValue("deviceId")         // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
173		attachmentID := r.PathValue("attachmentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty

224	// a 409. A successful or repeated finish returns the same recorded result.

227		attachmentID := r.PathValue("attachmentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty

252	// metadata, the sorted indices received so far and the completion status. The

323	// creator and any granted device see the same bytes. The judgments run in a
324	// fixed order: the path shape first (an empty identifier, a missing or extra
325	// segment and any non-GET method are a 400 JSON error enforced by the routing
326	// layer, all with zero writes), then an unknown or deleted attachment is a
327	// 404 JSON error, a caller that is neither the creator nor a granted reader
328	// is a 403 JSON error that leaks not a single byte, and an upload that is not
329	// sealed yet is a 409 JSON error that leaves the upload resumable. The
330	// content is assembled inside one serialized transaction, so a delete racing

332	// content. The endpoint is read-only: it writes nothing, allocates no cursor
333	// and notifies no subscriber, and repeated reads return the same bytes.
334	func handleGetAttachmentContent(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {

336		attachmentID := r.PathValue("attachmentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty

349			}

358	// handleListAttachmentAccess is the read-only roster over an attachment's
359	// access subresource: the device ids the attachment is currently open to for
360	// reading — every device the creator granted through the access endpoint and
361	// that has not been revoked — each at most once, ordered by the time their
362	// latest grant took effect ascending. The creator itself is not part of the
363	// roster (its reads come from ownership, so a self grant/revoke neither adds
364	// nor removes an entry). Only the attachment's creator may read it — the
365	// device in the path is the caller identity and there is no other
366	// authentication: an unknown or deleted attachment is a 404 and a non-creator
367	// caller a 403, judged independently. Pagination shares the attachment
368	// listing's limit/offset parsing, so an illegal value is a 400 checked before
369	// the attachment lookup. The handler writes nothing: no access row, chunk or
370	// attachment state changes.
371	func handleListAttachmentAccess(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
372		deviceID := r.PathValue("deviceId")         // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
373		attachmentID := r.PathValue("attachmentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
374	
375		limit, offset, ok := parseAttachmentListQuery(w, r)
376		if !ok {
377			return
378		}
379	
380		devices, err := s.ListAttachmentAccess(deviceID, attachmentID, limit, offset)
381		if err != nil {
382			switch {
383			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentNotFound):
384				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "attachment not found")
385			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentForbidden):
386				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "attachment belongs to another device")
387			default:
388				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to list attachment access")
389			}
390			return
391		}

393		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"devices": devices})
394	}
395	
396	// handleSetAttachmentAccess grants or revokes a registered device's read
397	// access to one attachment. Every (attachment, device) pair starts
398	// unauthorized, so the first grant is the first write; repeating the current
399	// state is idempotent (changed=false). Only the creator may change access: a
400	// non-creator caller gets a 403 and an unknown attachment a 404, neither
401	// touching any access state. A rejected request (bad content type, malformed
402	// JSON, trailing content, empty or mistyped fields, unknown action) is a 400
403	// JSON error and writes nothing; an unregistered target device is a 404 JSON
404	// error. A granted device reads the same metadata and chunk bytes as the
405	// creator; a revoke returns its reads to 403 at once and never deletes
406	// stored chunks or sealed content.
407	func handleSetAttachmentAccess(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
408		deviceID := r.PathValue("deviceId")         // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
409		attachmentID := r.PathValue("attachmentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
410	
411		var req permissionRequest
412		if !decodeJSONBody(w, r, &req) {
413			return
414		}
415		if req.DeviceID == "" {
416			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "deviceId must be a non-empty string")
417			return
418		}
419		var authorized bool
420		switch req.Action {
421		case "grant":
422			authorized = true
423		case "revoke":
424			authorized = false
425		default:
426			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, `action must be "grant" or "revoke"`)
427			return
428		}
429	
430		changed, err := s.SetAttachmentAccess(deviceID, attachmentID, req.DeviceID, authorized)
431		if err != nil {
432			switch {
433			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentNotFound):
434				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "attachment not found")
435			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentForbidden):
436				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "attachment belongs to another device")
437			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDeviceNotFound):
438				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "device not found")
439			default:
440				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to update attachment access")
441			}
442			return
443		}
444	
445		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{
446			"deviceId":   req.DeviceID,
447			"authorized": authorized,
448			"changed":    changed,
449		})
450	}
451	
452	// handleDeleteAttachment removes an upload outright. Only the creating device
453	// may delete: any other device gets a 403 and an unknown (or already deleted)
454	// id a 404, neither writing anything. A successful delete answers the
455	// attachment id and a deletion marker, after which the record, its chunks,
456	// its completion state and every access grant are gone: every later read,
457	// chunk write, finish or access change against the id is a 404, and
458	// re-creating the id starts a brand-new upload. Digest-addressed content is
459	// reclaimed only when no finished attachment references it any longer.
460	func handleDeleteAttachment(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
461		deviceID := r.PathValue("deviceId")         // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
462		attachmentID := r.PathValue("attachmentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
463	
464		if err := s.DeleteAttachment(deviceID, attachmentID); err != nil {
465			switch {
466			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentNotFound):
467				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "attachment not found")
468			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentForbidden):
469				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "attachment belongs to another device")
470			default:
471				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to delete attachment")
472			}
473			return
474		}
475	
476		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"attachmentId": attachmentID, "deleted": true})
477	}

479	// isLowerHexSHA256 reports whether s is exactly 64 lowercase hex characters.
480	func isLowerHexSHA256(s string) bool {
481		if len(s) != 64 {
482			return false
483		}
484		for _, c := range s {
485			if (c < '0' || c > '9') && (c < 'a' || c > 'f') {
486				return false
487			}
488		}
489		return true
490	}

1	// Package app is the composition root: it opens the one shared database and
2	// constructs the three independently reusable internal services — the change
3	// event service, the permission service and the CRDT state service — wiring
4	// them together only through their internal interfaces.
5	//
6	// The services share one SQLite connection (the kernel opens a single
7	// pooled connection with immediate transactions), so a change commit, a CRDT
8	// submission or compaction, and a permission change are serialized on the
9	// same connection and leave no half-written batch. The change event and CRDT
10	// services take their registration-and-authorization verdict from the
11	// permission service inside their own transactions (events.Gate / crdt.Gate),
12	// and the permission service fans a committed revoke out to their
13	// subscription registries through authz.RevokeSink. No service reaches into
14	// another service's tables or fields.
15	//
16	// App is the single object the entry and HTTP layers use. It promotes each
17	// service's input/output boundary as its methods while hiding the wiring; it
18	// adds no authentication and exposes no endpoint of its own.
19	package app
20	
21	import (
22		"context"
23		"encoding/json"
24		"time"
25	
26		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/authz"
27		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/crdt"
28		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/events"
29		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
30	)
31	
32	// App composes the durable kernel and the three internal services over one
33	// shared database connection.
34	type App struct {
35		*store.Store
36	
37		events *events.Service
38		crdt   *crdt.Service
39	
40		// Authz is the permission service. It is exposed so the HTTP layer can
41		// grant/revoke and read authorization directly; the other services reach
42		// it through their gates rather than this field.
43		Authz *authz.Service
44	}
45	
46	// Open opens (creating if needed) the SQLite database at path and constructs
47	// every internal service over it. The empty path opens a private in-memory
48	// database useful for tests. A construction failure closes the kernel and
49	// leaves nothing behind.
50	func Open(path string) (*App, error) {
51		kernel, err := store.Open(path)
52		if err != nil {
53			return nil, err
54		}
55	
56		// The permission service is built first: its gate is a constructor
57		// dependency of the change event and CRDT services.
58		permissions, err := authz.New(kernel)
59		if err != nil {
60			_ = kernel.Close()
61			return nil, err
62		}
63		eventService, err := events.New(kernel, permissions)
64		if err != nil {
65			_ = kernel.Close()
66			return nil, err
67		}
68		crdtService, err := crdt.New(kernel, permissions)
69		if err != nil {
70			_ = kernel.Close()
71			return nil, err
72		}
73	
74		// A committed revoke ends the affected live subscriptions in both
75		// push channels. The dependency is an interface, registered once here, so
76		// the permission service never names either subscriber concretely.
77		permissions.AddRevokeSink(eventsRevokeSink{eventService})
78		permissions.AddRevokeSink(crdtService)
79	
80		return &App{
81			Store:  kernel,
82			events: eventService,
83			crdt:   crdtService,
84			Authz:  permissions,
85		}, nil
86	}
87	
88	// eventsRevokeSink adapts the change event service's revoke hook to the
89	// permission service's RevokeSink interface.
90	type eventsRevokeSink struct{ e *events.Service }
91	
92	func (s eventsRevokeSink) PermissionRevoked(documentID, deviceID string) {
93		s.e.SignalRevoked(documentID, deviceID)
94	}
95	
96	// Events returns the change event service.
97	func (a *App) Events() *events.Service { return a.events }
98	
99	// CRDT returns the CRDT state service.
100	func (a *App) CRDT() *crdt.Service { return a.crdt }
101	
102	// ---- Change event service boundary (promoted so the entry layer has one
103	// object; each method delegates verbatim to the events service). ----
104	
105	// InterruptWaits wakes every parked long poll and every live change-log and
106	// CRDT subscription without closing the database, so an orderly shutdown
107	// drains waiting connections (long polls answer 503; subscriptions finish
108	// with the going-away close) instead of holding the drain hostage.
109	func (a *App) InterruptWaits() {
110		a.events.InterruptWaits()
111		a.crdt.InterruptWaits()
112	}
113	
114	// Closing reports whether shutdown has begun, covering both push channels.
115	func (a *App) Closing() bool {
116		return a.events.Closing() || a.crdt.Closing()
117	}
118	
119	// Close interrupts the in-memory observers, waits for every subscription
120	// handler to unregister and then releases the shared database handle.
121	func (a *App) Close() error {
122		a.events.InterruptWaits()
123		a.crdt.InterruptWaits()
124		a.events.WaitDrained()
125		a.crdt.WaitDrained()
126		return a.Store.Close()
127	}
128	
129	// PostChanges delegates to the change event service.
130	func (a *App) PostChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
131		return a.events.PostChanges(documentID, changes)
132	}
133	
134	// ReplayChanges delegates to the change event service.
135	func (a *App) ReplayChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
136		return a.events.ReplayChanges(documentID, changes)
137	}
138	
139	// MergeChange delegates to the change event service.
140	func (a *App) MergeChange(documentID string, baseCursor int64, c events.Change) (events.MergeResult, error) {
141		return a.events.MergeChange(documentID, baseCursor, c)
142	}
143	
144	// PutSnapshot delegates to the change event service.
145	func (a *App) PutSnapshot(documentID string, cursor int64, state json.RawMessage) (bool, error) {
146		return a.events.PutSnapshot(documentID, cursor, state)
147	}
148	
149	// GetSnapshot delegates to the change event service.
150	func (a *App) GetSnapshot(documentID string, cursor int64) (json.RawMessage, error) {
151		return a.events.GetSnapshot(documentID, cursor)
152	}
153	
154	// ExportSnapshots delegates to the change event service. A nil to means the
155	// interval has no upper bound.
156	func (a *App) ExportSnapshots(documentID string, from int64, to *int64) ([]events.ExportedSnapshot, error) {
157		return a.events.ExportSnapshots(documentID, from, to)
158	}
159	
160	// RestoreSnapshot delegates to the change event service.
161	func (a *App) RestoreSnapshot(documentID, deviceID, changeID string, snapshotCursor int64) (events.RestoreResult, error) {
162		return a.events.RestoreSnapshot(documentID, deviceID, changeID, snapshotCursor)
163	}
164	
165	// ListChanges delegates to the change event service.
166	func (a *App) ListChanges(documentID string, after, limit int64) ([]events.ListedChange, int64, error) {
167		return a.events.ListChanges(documentID, after, limit)
168	}
169	
170	// WaitForChanges delegates to the change event service.
171	func (a *App) WaitForChanges(ctx context.Context, documentID string, after, limit int64, wait time.Duration) ([]events.ListedChange, int64, bool, error) {
172		return a.events.WaitForChanges(ctx, documentID, after, limit, wait)
173	}
174	
175	// DocumentExists delegates to the change event service.
176	func (a *App) DocumentExists(documentID string) (bool, error) {
177		return a.events.DocumentExists(documentID)
178	}
179	
180	// CompactChanges delegates to the change event service.
181	func (a *App) CompactChanges(documentID, deviceID string) (boundary, removed int64, err error) {
182		return a.events.CompactChanges(documentID, deviceID)
183	}
184	
185	// AddSubscription delegates to the change event service.
186	func (a *App) AddSubscription(documentID, deviceID string) (<-chan struct{}, <-chan struct{}, func()) {
187		return a.events.AddSubscription(documentID, deviceID)
188	}
189	
190	// DeregisterDevice removes a registered device together with every record it
191	// owns — its sessions, the attachments it created (chunks, sealed state and
192	// unfinished uploads included), the access grants it held, and its
193	// document-permission rows — all in one serialized transaction that commits
194	// synchronously. An unknown or already deregistered device yields
195	// store.ErrDeviceNotFound and writes nothing, so a repeat deregistration
196	// misses exactly the way a never-registered id does and concurrent calls take
197	// effect at most once. Shared digest-addressed content is reclaimed only when
198	// the last completed attachment referencing it is gone; other devices'
199	// changes, snapshots and document content are untouched.
200	//
201	// After the commit the same id may register again as a brand-new device — no
202	// session, permission or attachment is inherited — and every live
203	// subscription the device held across both push channels is ended
204	// immediately, stickily.
205	func (a *App) DeregisterDevice(deviceID string) error {
206		tx, err := a.Store.DB().Begin()
207		if err != nil {
208			return err
209		}
210		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
211	
212		if err := store.DeleteDeviceTx(tx, deviceID); err != nil {
213			return err
214		}
215		if err := a.Authz.DeleteDevicePermissionsTx(tx, deviceID); err != nil {
216			return err
217		}
218		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
219			return err
220		}
221	
222		// End the device's live subscriptions only after the cascade is durable:
223		// a reconnect attempt after the close finds the backing session gone
224		// (404), so the connection cannot immediately re-establish itself.
225		a.events.SignalDeviceDeregistered(deviceID)
226		a.crdt.SignalDeviceDeregistered(deviceID)
227		return nil
228	}

230	// ---- Permission service boundary. ----
231	
232	// SetDocumentPermission delegates to the permission service.
233	func (a *App) SetDocumentPermission(documentID, deviceID string, authorized bool) (bool, error) {
234		return a.Authz.SetDocumentPermission(documentID, deviceID, authorized)
235	}

238	func (a *App) DocumentAuthorized(documentID, deviceID string) (bool, error) {
239		return a.Authz.DocumentAuthorized(documentID, deviceID)
240	}

243	
244	// SubmitCRDTOps delegates to the CRDT state service.
245	func (a *App) SubmitCRDTOps(documentID, declaredType string, ops []crdt.Op) ([]crdt.Result, error) {

252	}

256		return a.crdt.Compact(documentID, deviceID)
257	}

260	func (a *App) GetCRDTSnapshot(documentID string) (crdt.Snapshot, error) {
261		return a.crdt.GetSnapshot(documentID)
262	}

265	func (a *App) OpenCRDTSubscription(documentID, deviceID string) (*crdt.State, *crdt.Subscription, func(), error) {

1	// Package store is the durable kernel shared by the internal services: it
2	// owns the SQLite database handle and the registration layer (devices and
3	// sessions) plus resumable attachments.
4	//
5	// The business services layered on top of the kernel — the change event log,
6	// the permission ledger and the CRDT state — live in their own packages and
7	// cooperate only through their internal interfaces. They all share this one
8	// handle: it opens a single pooled connection with immediate write
9	// transactions, so every service's transactional judgment is serialized on
10	// the same connection and no batch is ever half written.
11	//
12	// Devices and sessions form the registration layer. A device registers with a
13	// client-supplied id; a session belongs to exactly one registered device and
14	// is addressed by its own client-supplied id. Registration and session
15	// creation are idempotent re-posts: the first call creates, an identical
16	// repeat does not. A session id already owned by another device is a
17	// conflict, never silently re-homed. Deletes are owner-scoped and hard: a
18	// repeat delete, another device, and a cross-device path all miss with 404,
19	// after which the id is free to be created again. A device itself can
20	// deregister: the device row and everything it owns — its sessions and the
21	// attachments it created, chunks and grants included — vanish in one
22	// serialized transaction, a repeat or never-registered deregistration misses
23	// with 404 and writes nothing, and the freed id registers again as a
24	// brand-new device.
25	//
26	// Attachments are resumable chunked uploads owned by the registered device
27	// that created them. Creation pins the declared total size, chunk size and
28	// SHA-256 digest; chunks land in any order and are stored durably as they
29	// arrive, so an interrupted upload resumes after a restart with its
30	// idempotency and conflict decisions intact. Finishing concatenates the
31	// chunks, verifies the digest and seals the upload; a sealed upload is
32	// immutable and rejects every further chunk write. Finished content is
33	// addressed by digest, so a second attachment with the same digest and size
34	// reuses the stored bytes instead of copying them. The creator may grant
35	// other registered devices read-only access per attachment; every
36	// (attachment, device) pair starts unauthorized, grants and revokes commit in
37	// the same serialized way, and access never widens the write paths. Deletes
38	// are owner-scoped and hard: the record, its chunks and its grants vanish in
39	// one serialized transaction, a repeat delete misses with 404, the id is free
40	// to be created again, and the shared content bytes are reclaimed once the
41	// last completed attachment referencing them is gone.
42	package store
43	
44	import (
45		"database/sql"
46		"encoding/json"
47		"errors"
48		"fmt"
49	
50		_ "modernc.org/sqlite"
51	)
52	
53	// ErrDeviceNotFound reports that an operation targets a device id that was
54	// never registered. Services map it to 404; nothing is written.
55	var ErrDeviceNotFound = errors.New("device not found")
56	
57	// ErrPermissionDenied reports that a device's access to a document has been
58	// revoked. Services map it to 403; nothing is written and no document content
59	// is exposed. It is a shared verdict produced by the permission service and
60	// consulted by every service that enforces the gate inside a transaction.
61	var ErrPermissionDenied = errors.New("device permission for this document has been revoked")
62	
63	// ErrSessionConflict reports that a session id already belongs to a different
64	// device. The session keeps its original owner; nothing is written. Services
65	// map it to 409.
66	type ErrSessionConflict struct {
67		ID string
68	}
69	
70	func (e *ErrSessionConflict) Error() string {
71		return fmt.Sprintf("session %q belongs to another device", e.ID)
72	}
73	
74	// ErrSessionNotFound reports that no live session matches the (device,
75	// session) pair: the session was never created, was already deleted, or
76	// belongs to another device. Services map it to 404.
77	var ErrSessionNotFound = errors.New("session not found")
78	
79	// DBTX is the subset of *sql.DB and *sql.Tx the services use for their
80	// serialized work, so judgments made "in the same transaction" (for example a
81	// permission gate followed by the gated write) run on one concrete connection
82	// whether the caller holds a transaction or the handle itself.
83	type DBTX interface {
84		Exec(query string, args ...any) (sql.Result, error)
85		Query(query string, args ...any) (*sql.Rows, error)
86		QueryRow(query string, args ...any) *sql.Row
87	}
88	
89	// Store is the durable kernel: one SQLite database handle together with the
90	// device, session and attachment data it owns.
91	type Store struct {
92		db *sql.DB
93	}
94	
95	// Open opens (creating if needed) the SQLite database at path. The empty path
96	// opens an in-memory database useful for tests.
97	func Open(path string) (*Store, error) {
98		if path == "" {
99			// With a single pooled connection this is a private, per-instance
100			// in-memory database (useful for tests).
101			path = "file::memory:"
102		}
103		// _txlock=immediate makes writers acquire the write lock at BEGIN, so
104		// concurrent batches serialize without SQLITE_BUSY deadlocks.
105		dsn := path + "?_txlock=immediate&_busy_timeout=5000&_journal_mode=WAL&_synchronous=FULL&_foreign_keys=on"
106		db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", dsn)
107		if err != nil {
108			return nil, err
109		}
110		// One connection avoids cross-connection locking surprises; writes are
111		// serialized by the immediate transaction anyway, and SQLite concurrency
112		// for readers does not help correctness here. It also keeps every
113		// service's transaction serialized on the same connection.
114		db.SetMaxOpenConns(1)
115		s := &Store{db: db}
116		if err := s.init(); err != nil {
117			_ = db.Close()
118			return nil, err
119		}
120		return s, nil
121	}
122	
123	// DB returns the underlying handle. The business services use it to open the
124	// serialized transactions their judgments run in; callers outside the
125	// internal packages never need it.
126	func (s *Store) DB() *sql.DB { return s.db }
127	
128	// Close releases the database handle.
129	func (s *Store) Close() error {
130		return s.db.Close()
131	}
132	
133	func (s *Store) init() error {
134		_, err := s.db.Exec(`
135	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS devices (
136		id TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY
137	);
138	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sessions (
139		id        TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
140		device_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES devices(id)
141	);
142	CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS sessions_device_idx
143		ON sessions(device_id);
144	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS attachments (
145		id          TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
146		device_id   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES devices(id),
147		total_bytes INTEGER NOT NULL,
148		chunk_size  INTEGER NOT NULL,
149		sha256      TEXT NOT NULL,
150		complete    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
151		reused      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
152		created_seq INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
153	);
154	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS attachment_chunks (
155		attachment_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES attachments(id),
156		idx           INTEGER NOT NULL,
157		data          BLOB NOT NULL,
158		PRIMARY KEY (attachment_id, idx)
159	);
160	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS attachment_contents (
161		sha256 TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
162		size   INTEGER NOT NULL,
163		data   BLOB NOT NULL
164	);
165	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS attachment_access (
166		attachment_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES attachments(id),
167		device_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
168		authorized    INTEGER NOT NULL,
169		granted_seq   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
170		PRIMARY KEY (attachment_id, device_id)
171	);
172	`)
173		if err != nil {
174			return err
175		}
176		if err := s.ensureAttachmentCreatedSeq(); err != nil {
177			return err
178		}
179		return s.ensureAttachmentAccessGrantedSeq()
180	}
181	
182	// ensureAttachmentCreatedSeq adds the creation-order column to databases
183	// created before it existed. Existing rows are backfilled in insertion
184	// (rowid) order so their relative listing order is unchanged; new rows take
185	// strictly larger values, so the sequence never reuses a value even after
186	// the newest attachment is deleted and its id created again.
187	func (s *Store) ensureAttachmentCreatedSeq() error {
188		rows, err := s.db.Query(`PRAGMA table_info(attachments)`)
189		if err != nil {
190			return err
191		}
192		hasColumn := false
193		for rows.Next() {
194			var cid, notNull, pk int
195			var name, colType string
196			var dflt sql.NullString
197			if err := rows.Scan(&cid, &name, &colType, &notNull, &dflt, &pk); err != nil {
198				_ = rows.Close()
199				return err
200			}
201			if name == "created_seq" {
202				hasColumn = true
203			}
204		}
205		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
206			_ = rows.Close()
207			return err
208		}
209		_ = rows.Close()
210		if hasColumn {
211			return nil
212		}
213		if _, err := s.db.Exec(
214			`ALTER TABLE attachments ADD COLUMN created_seq INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`,
215		); err != nil {
216			return err
217		}
218		_, err = s.db.Exec(
219			`UPDATE attachments SET created_seq = (
220				SELECT COUNT(*) FROM attachments older WHERE older.rowid <= attachments.rowid
221			)`,
222		)
223		return err
224	}
225	
226	// ensureAttachmentAccessGrantedSeq adds the grant-order column to access
227	// tables created before it existed. Existing rows are backfilled one past the
228	// per-attachment maximum in insertion (rowid) order, so surviving grants keep
229	// a stable relative order; every new grant takes a strictly larger value, even
230	// after the previously newest grant was revoked, so a re-granted device lists
231	// at the position of its latest grant and a value is never reused.

268					FROM attachment_access

276	// an id creates it and reports created=true; repeating the registration is
277	// idempotent (created=false). Device identity never changes.

279		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
280		if err != nil {
281			return false, err
282		}
283		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
284	
285		created, err = RegisterDeviceTx(tx, deviceID)
286		if err != nil {
287			return false, err
288		}
289		return created, tx.Commit()

293	// services can resolve the registration layer as the first step of a larger
294	// serialized transaction (their permission/content gates then share it).
295	func RegisterDeviceTx(q DBTX, deviceID string) (created bool, err error) {
296		var exists bool

299		).Scan(&exists); err != nil {

302		if !exists {
303			if _, err := q.Exec(`INSERT INTO devices (id) VALUES (?)`, deviceID); err != nil {
304				return false, err

306			return true, nil

323	// CreateSession creates a session owned by deviceID with a client-supplied id.
324	//
325	//   - An unknown device yields ErrDeviceNotFound; nothing is written.
326	//   - A session id already owned by another device yields *ErrSessionConflict;
327	//     nothing is written and the owner is unchanged.
328	//   - Re-posting the same (device, session) pair is idempotent: created=false.
329	//
330	// A deleted session is gone for good, so its id can be registered again as a
331	// brand-new session (created=true). The lookup, owner check and insert run in
332	// one serialized transaction, so concurrent creates of the same session id
333	// cannot both create it.
334	func (s *Store) CreateSession(deviceID, sessionID string) (created bool, err error) {
335		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
336		if err != nil {
337			return false, err
338		}
339		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
340	
341		var deviceExists bool
342		if err := tx.QueryRow(
343			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM devices WHERE id = ?)`, deviceID,
344		).Scan(&deviceExists); err != nil {
345			return false, err
346		}
347		if !deviceExists {
348			return false, ErrDeviceNotFound
349		}
350	
351		var owner string
352		err = tx.QueryRow(
353			`SELECT device_id FROM sessions WHERE id = ?`, sessionID,
354		).Scan(&owner)
355		switch {
356		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
357			if _, err := tx.Exec(
358				`INSERT INTO sessions (id, device_id) VALUES (?, ?)`,
359				sessionID, deviceID,
360			); err != nil {
361				return false, err
362			}
363			if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
364				return false, err
365			}
366			return true, nil
367		case err != nil:
368			return false, err
369		}
370	
371		if owner != deviceID {
372			return false, &ErrSessionConflict{ID: sessionID}
373		}
374		return false, tx.Commit()
375	}

377	// DeleteSession removes the live session matching the (deviceID, sessionID)
378	// pair. Any miss — the session does not exist, was already deleted, or belongs
379	// to another device — returns ErrSessionNotFound and changes nothing. The
380	// check and the delete run in one transaction, so a concurrent create cannot
381	// interleave and a repeat delete still misses; the removal is committed to
382	// disk before the call returns.
383	func (s *Store) DeleteSession(deviceID, sessionID string) error {
384		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
385		if err != nil {
386			return err
387		}
388		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
389	
390		var owner string
391		err = tx.QueryRow(
392			`SELECT device_id FROM sessions WHERE id = ?`, sessionID,
393		).Scan(&owner)
394		switch {
395		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
396			return ErrSessionNotFound
397		case err != nil:
398			return err
399		}
400		if owner != deviceID {
401			return ErrSessionNotFound
402		}
403	
404		if _, err := tx.Exec(
405			`DELETE FROM sessions WHERE id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
406			sessionID, deviceID,
407		); err != nil {
408			return err
409		}
410		return tx.Commit()
411	}

413	// DeleteDeviceTx deregisters deviceID and removes every record it owns, all
414	// inside the caller's serialized transaction:
415	//
416	//   - the device's sessions are hard-deleted, so their session-scoped reads
417	//     and subscriptions miss from then on;
418	//   - every attachment it created is removed together with its chunks, its
419	//     sealed/unfinished state and the access rows other devices held on it;
420	//   - the read grants the device itself held on other devices' attachments
421	//     are withdrawn;
422	//   - the device row is removed last (every child row goes first).
423	//
424	// Digest-addressed content is shared across attachments and is reclaimed only
425	// when no completed attachment still references a digest — exactly the rule
426	// of a single attachment delete — so another device's attachment with the same
427	// digest keeps its bytes and one deregistration by itself never reclaims
428	// shared content. The document permission ledger lives in the authz package
429	// and clears its own rows against the same transaction through
430	// DeleteDevicePermissionsTx.
431	//
432	// An unknown (never registered or already deregistered) device yields
433	// ErrDeviceNotFound and writes nothing. Because the whole judgment runs in one
434	// immediate transaction on the single shared connection, concurrent
435	// deregistrations of the same device commit at most once and any concurrent
436	// chunk upload or finish either committed entirely before it or is rejected
437	// entirely afterward — no half-written record survives.
438	func DeleteDeviceTx(q DBTX, deviceID string) error {
439		exists, err := DeviceExistsTx(q, deviceID)
440		if err != nil {
441			return err
442		}
443		if !exists {
444			return ErrDeviceNotFound
445		}
446	
447		// Remember the digests of the device's completed attachments before their
448		// rows vanish: each is a candidate for content reclamation once every
449		// owned attachment is gone. DISTINCT because several of the device's
450		// attachments may share the same digest-addressed content.
451		rows, err := q.Query(
452			`SELECT DISTINCT sha256 FROM attachments WHERE device_id = ? AND complete = 1`,
453			deviceID,
454		)
455		if err != nil {
456			return err
457		}
458		var digests []string
459		for rows.Next() {
460			var digest string
461			if err := rows.Scan(&digest); err != nil {
462				_ = rows.Close()
463				return err
464			}
465			digests = append(digests, digest)
466		}
467		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
468			_ = rows.Close()
469			return err
470		}
471		if err := rows.Close(); err != nil {
472			return err
473		}
474	
475		// Withdraw the read grants this device held on other devices'
476		// attachments (rows naming it as the grantee), then remove the access
477		// rosters of the attachments it created before the attachment rows those
478		// rosters reference are deleted.
479		if _, err := q.Exec(
480			`DELETE FROM attachment_access WHERE device_id = ?`, deviceID,
481		); err != nil {
482			return err
483		}
484		if _, err := q.Exec(
485			`DELETE FROM attachment_access
486			 WHERE attachment_id IN (SELECT id FROM attachments WHERE device_id = ?)`,
487			deviceID,
488		); err != nil {
489			return err
490		}
491		if _, err := q.Exec(
492			`DELETE FROM attachment_chunks
493			 WHERE attachment_id IN (SELECT id FROM attachments WHERE device_id = ?)`,
494			deviceID,
495		); err != nil {
496			return err
497		}
498		if _, err := q.Exec(
499			`DELETE FROM attachments WHERE device_id = ?`, deviceID,
500		); err != nil {
501			return err
502		}
503	
504		// Reclaim each digest-addressed content only when no surviving completed
505		// attachment — owned by another device, or by the deregistered device in
506		// an impossible re-read — still references it.
507		for _, digest := range digests {
508			var stillReferenced bool
509			if err := q.QueryRow(
510				`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM attachments WHERE sha256 = ? AND complete = 1)`,
511				digest,
512			).Scan(&stillReferenced); err != nil {
513				return err
514			}
515			if !stillReferenced {
516				if _, err := q.Exec(
517					`DELETE FROM attachment_contents WHERE sha256 = ?`, digest,
518				); err != nil {
519					return err
520				}
521			}
522		}
523	
524		if _, err := q.Exec(
525			`DELETE FROM sessions WHERE device_id = ?`, deviceID,
526		); err != nil {
527			return err
528		}
529		if _, err := q.Exec(
530			`DELETE FROM devices WHERE id = ?`, deviceID,
531		); err != nil {
532			return err
533		}
534		return nil
535	}

539	// require that the session currently exists.

541		var exists bool
542		if err := s.db.QueryRow(
543			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM sessions WHERE id = ?)`, sessionID,
544		).Scan(&exists); err != nil {

546		}
547		return exists, nil
548	}

554		var deviceID string
555		err := s.db.QueryRow(
556			`SELECT device_id FROM sessions WHERE id = ?`, sessionID,
557		).Scan(&deviceID)
558		switch {
559		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
560			return "", ErrSessionNotFound
561		case err != nil:
562			return "", err
563		default:
564			return deviceID, nil
565		}
566	}

568	// JSONEqual reports whether two payloads are equal after JSON decoding, so
569	// 1 and 1.0, or {"a":1,"b":2} and {"b":2,"a":1}, compare equal. It is shared
570	// verbatim by the change event and CRDT services' idempotency judgments.
571	func JSONEqual(a, b json.RawMessage) bool {
572		var va, vb any
573		if err := json.Unmarshal(a, &va); err != nil {
574			return false
575		}
576		if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &vb); err != nil {
577			return false
578		}
579		return deepEqual(va, vb)
580	}

582	func deepEqual(a, b any) bool {
583		switch av := a.(type) {
584		case nil:
585			return b == nil
586		case bool:
587			bv, ok := b.(bool)
588			return ok && av == bv
589		case string:
590			bv, ok := b.(string)
591			return ok && av == bv
592		case float64:
593			bv, ok := b.(float64)
594			return ok && av == bv
595		case []any:
596			bv, ok := b.([]any)
597			if !ok || len(av) != len(bv) {
598				return false
599			}
600			for i := range av {
601				if !deepEqual(av[i], bv[i]) {
602					return false
603				}
604			}
605			return true
606		case map[string]any:
607			bv, ok := b.(map[string]any)
608			if !ok || len(av) != len(bv) {
609				return false
610			}
611			for k, v := range av {
612				w, exists := bv[k]
613				if !exists || !deepEqual(v, w) {
614					return false
615				}
616			}
617			return true
618		default:
619			return false
620		}
621	}

266	// "crdt" segment in any position short of that shape is a malformed 400 rather
267	// than ServeMux's redirect or plain-text 404/405, so the new endpoints never
268	// redirect or emit HTML. The keyword is matched only past the documentID
269	// position, so a document literally named "crdt" keeps its ordinary routes.
270	func malformedCRDTPath(p string) bool {
271		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/documents/")
272		if !ok {
273			return false
274		}
275		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
276		for i, seg := range segs {
277			if seg == "crdt" && i > 0 {
278				if len(segs) != 3 || segs[0] == "" {
279					return true
280				}
281				switch segs[2] {
282				case "ops", "state", "compact", "snapshot":
283					return false
284				default:
285					return true
286				}
287			}
288		}
289		return false
290	}
